observations.text: SP completed the circling approach only with the IP directing the offset downwind spacing and flying part of the base turn to align the aircraft for landing. Airspeed deviation reached 24 knots and the circling altitude was deviated by 340 feet before the IP intervened. Performance meets the block MIF of 0 but remains marginal for the Training Section. Review of the MAIP circling procedure and of the visual references for the base turn is expected to reduce the dependence on IP direction.

SP flew the circling approach and aligned with the landing runway using only the IP's verbal prompts on downwind spacing, with no control input from him. Airspeed deviation reached the 20 knot limit and altitude deviation the 300 foot limit, with the corrections applied after the prompt was given. Above end of block MIF achieved.

SP flew the published MAIP circling pattern and aligned with the landing runway without IP intervention, recognizing the wide offset downwind on his own initiative. Airspeed deviation did not exceed 16 knots and altitude deviation stayed within 210 feet of the circling altitude, both corrected in a timely manner. Above end of block MIF achieved.

SP executed the circling approach according to the standardized procedure, maintained visual contact with the runway environment throughout and followed the ATC directives with precision. Airspeed was held within 8 knots and the circling altitude within 120 feet, with the aircraft aligned for landing before the descent from the circling altitude was started. Above end of block MIF achieved.

SP flew the circling maneuver at the published minimum altitude without violating it, with the base turn started at the briefed visual reference and the roll-out on the extended runway centerline. Airspeed varied by no more than 4 knots and altitude by no more than 40 feet until the final descent was started. Above end of block MIF achieved.

SP, due to an offset downwind flown wider than the distance published in the MAIP, did not place the aircraft in a position that allowed a normal base turn and rolled out displaced from the extended runway centerline. The overshoot was corrected with increasing bank and the circling altitude was deviated by 380 feet, beyond the 300 foot limit, with the result that the IP took control and repositioned the aircraft for the final turn.

SP, due to an interrupted instrument cross-check while attention remained outside on the runway environment, did not monitor the airspeed during the base turn and allowed it to decay below the circling speed. Airspeed deviation reached 26 knots, beyond the 20 knot limit, with the result that the IP added power and flew part of the turn to align the aircraft with the landing runway.

SP completed the circling approach and aligned for landing after the IP's verbal prompts on the base turn point and on the power setting. Airspeed deviation reached the 20 knot limit and altitude deviation the 300 foot limit, recognized and corrected with delay. Performance meets the block MIF of 1 but remains marginal for the Training Section. Anticipation of the base turn at the briefed visual reference is expected to remove the need for prompting.

SP flew the circling pattern within the track published in the MAIP and aligned with the landing runway without IP intervention. Airspeed deviation reached 15 knots during the base turn and altitude deviation 190 feet, both recognized and corrected in a timely manner on his own initiative. Above end of block MIF achieved.

SP executed the circling approach according to the standardized procedure, kept the runway environment in sight and complied with the ATC circling direction with precision. Airspeed was maintained within 9 knots and the circling altitude within 130 feet, and the aircraft was aligned for landing before the descent was started. Above end of block MIF achieved.

SP flew the offset downwind, the base turn and the roll-out exactly as published in the MAIP, without violating the circling minimum altitude at any point. Airspeed varied by no more than 5 knots and altitude by no more than 50 feet, and the touchdown was made within 1000 feet of the beginning of the runway on the centerline. Above end of block MIF achieved.

SP, due to a power reduction made before the aircraft was in the landing configuration, did not maintain the circling airspeed in the turn to base and did not arrest the resulting sink. Altitude deviation reached 350 feet and the aircraft descended below the published circling minimum altitude, with the result that the IP took control to stop the descent and re-establish the pattern.

SP, due to continuation bias in maintaining the approach after the conditions had deteriorated below the briefed minima, did not initiate the missed approach when the runway environment was lost in the base turn and continued the circling maneuver. Airspeed deviation reached 25 knots and altitude deviation 330 feet while the runway was being searched for, with the result that the IP directed the go-around and flew the initial climb.

SP, due to a base turn started later than the visual reference published in the MAIP, did not complete the alignment with the landing runway before roll-out and had to correct the overshoot on final. Airspeed reached the 20 knot limit during the correction, and the deviation was recognized and corrected only after the IP's verbal prompt. No control input by the IP was required.

SP, due to inadequate workload management during the approach phase, did not complete the landing checks before starting the base turn and flew the turn with attention divided between the checklist and the runway environment. Altitude deviation reached the 300 foot limit and was corrected with delay, following the IP's verbal prompt. The aircraft was aligned for landing without IP control input.

SP flew the circling approach within the desired standards and aligned for landing without IP intervention; however, altitude deviation twice reached 230 feet on the offset downwind before being corrected. The circling track published in the MAIP and the ATC directives were followed throughout, and the minimum altitude was not violated. Performance meets the block MIF of 2 but remains marginal for the Training Section. Stabilizing the power setting before the base turn is expected to reduce the altitude excursions.

SP executed the circling approach in accordance with the Flight Manual and the procedure published in the MAIP, without mistakes and without IP intervention. Airspeed was held within 7 knots and the circling altitude within 110 feet, with the aircraft aligned with the landing runway before the final descent. Above end of block MIF achieved.

SP flew the entire circling maneuver at the published minimum altitude, with the base turn and the roll-out placed exactly as briefed and with continuous visual contact with the runway environment. Altitude varied by no more than 40 feet and airspeed by no more than 4 knots, and the touchdown was made within 1000 feet of the beginning of the runway on the centerline. Above end of block MIF achieved.

SP, due to a descent started from the circling altitude before the aircraft was aligned with the landing runway, did not respect the published circling minimum altitude and continued the descent inside the turn. Altitude deviation reached 400 feet below the circling altitude, beyond the 300 foot limit, with the result that the IP took control and climbed the aircraft back to the minimum altitude.

SP, due to loss of situational awareness of the aircraft's position in the pattern at night, did not fly the circling maneuver on the side of the runway specified by ATC and turned base from a position that did not comply with the MAIP procedure. Airspeed deviation reached 27 knots during the late correction, with the result that the IP took control and repositioned the aircraft for a second circling approach.

SP, due to a power setting that was not adjusted after the configuration change, did not maintain the circling airspeed on the offset downwind and allowed the aircraft to accelerate through the base turn. Airspeed deviation reached the 20 knot limit and was recognized and corrected only after the IP's verbal prompt. Alignment with the landing runway was completed without IP control input.

SP, due to distraction by radio traffic while flying the offset downwind, did not maintain the circling altitude and did not re-establish the cross-check before starting the base turn. Altitude deviation reached the 300 foot limit and was corrected with delay after the IP's verbal prompt. The minimum altitude was not violated and no IP control input was required.

SP, due to a base turn flown with less bank than the wind conditions required, did not complete the alignment with the landing runway before roll-out and had to correct a displacement from the extended centerline. Altitude deviation reached 240 feet during the correction and airspeed deviation 14 knots, both recognized and corrected in a timely manner without IP intervention.

SP, due to an incomplete mental model of the approach sequence that was not updated when the clearance changed, did not fly the circling side ordered by ATC at the first call and started the offset downwind on the opposite side. The error was self-detected before the base turn and the published pattern was re-established with altitude deviation limited to 200 feet and airspeed deviation to 13 knots, without IP intervention.

SP executed the circling approach according to the standardized procedure, without violating the minimum altitude and without IP intervention, holding airspeed within 9 knots and the circling altitude within 140 feet. The base turn was nevertheless started slightly late on both attempts and the roll-out required a correction toward the extended centerline. Performance meets the block MIF of 3 but remains marginal for the Training Section. Consistency in identifying the base turn reference is expected to improve over the remaining sorties of the block.

SP flew the circling approach with the offset downwind, the base turn and the roll-out placed exactly as published in the MAIP, following the ATC directives with precision and keeping the runway environment in sight throughout. Airspeed varied by no more than 4 knots and the circling altitude by no more than 40 feet, and the touchdown was made within 1000 feet of the beginning of the runway and within 5 feet of the centerline. Above end of block MIF achieved.
